root_cause_label: Agent chose a heavyweight GPU torch install (full CUDA stack) rather than a CPU-only index, triggering a >2GB multi-package download that the agent could not supervise: it issued 12 empty/N/A steps (5-16), then further confused commands and a spurious Ctrl+C (17-24), wasting ~20 steps on idle waiting and desynchronization before recovering.
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent installed the full GPU torch stack instead of a lightweight CPU-only build, causing a prolonged download that the agent could not supervise properly — it spent steps 5-24 issuing empty commands and losing terminal synchronization rather than doing useful parallel work, ultimately consuming the step budget before the pipeline could reliably complete within time constraints.
t_err_evidence: pip install torch transformers peft accelerate
t_commit_evidence: Step 5: the agent issues no command ('N/A') and begins passive idle waiting as the 899 MB torch wheel downloads. From this point the agent's actual behavior (12+ empty/N/A steps, spurious Ctrl+C, echo placeholders) locks in a trajectory of wasted budget. Given the agent's behavior pattern through step 24, the failing outcome (task timeout / incomplete execution within the step budget) was inevitable.
t_surface_evidence: ImportError: XLMRobertaTokenizer requires the SentencePiece library but it was not found in your environment.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacked domain knowledge on two fronts: (1) it did not know to use a CPU-only torch install index (--index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu) to avoid pulling gigabytes of CUDA wheels in a likely CPU-only container environment, and (2) it did not know that XLMRobertaTokenizer requires sentencepiece as an additional dependency not bundled with transformers. The first gap caused the massive install that the agent could not properly supervise; the second caused a direct script failure at step 30.
